simple.meaning: זָחַח (zâchach) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to shove or displace.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Exodus, beginning at Exodus 28:28. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זָחַח (H2118) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: זָחַח (zâchach) / H2118 is traced through Exodus 28:28, Exodus 39:21 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: They shall bind the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it may be on the skillfully woven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate may not swing out from the ephod.
